'''Starweirds''' were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of incorporeal [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] [[Vacuumbreather|found only]] in [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. Tall and gaunt, they possessed long, sharp talons, wild [[Color/Legends|white]] hair, and glowing [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. The creatures appeared to [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] repairing their [[Starship/Legends|starships]] in space, or aboard vessels traveling through [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. A starweird would choose a target, and, after being spotted, emit a [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathic]] scream that terrified most individuals. The starweird would then attack its victim. Starweirds were powerful creatures capable of using [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], and held a strong hatred for [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force users]], leading some [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] to believe that they were apparitions created by the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. During the time of the [[Great Galactic War|first conflict]] fought between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Wyellett]] saved his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Xerender]] and many members of the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] from a famous starweird known as the [[Starweird Queen]].

==Biology and appearance==
Starweirds were incorporeal, [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]], [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-using]] creatures [[Vacuumbreather|found only]] in the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. They were very tall and extremely gaunt&mdash;to the point of almost being [[Bone/Legends|skeletal]]&mdash;and wore ephemeral rags that hung from their two [[Limb/Legends|arms]]. Starweirds had long, wild [[Color/Legends|white]] hair that floated around their heads even when influenced by [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]]. The creatures had pale skin that varied slightly in color from one starweird to another, and their faces were desiccated. However, specific accounts of what a starweird's face looked like varied, with many witnesses stating that the creature's face somewhat resembled their own. Starweirds each had a large, [[Tooth/Legends|toothy]] [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]] and [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] that glowed in a way that some individuals described as eerie. Their arms were bony and ended in hands with three large, sharp, black talons. The species' incorporeal nature made it possible for the creature to resist conventional attacks and pass through solid objects, although [[Force field/Legends|force fields]] still stopped the creatures. They were also fully affected by the [[Force power/Legends|use of the Force]].<ref name="UA" />

Instead of walking on their two legs, Starweirds hovered or flew silently at a speed that was slightly faster than most bipedal [[Human/Legends|Human]]-sized species could move. While fairly intelligent, the creatures did not speak or communicate and had no known [[Language/Legends|language]]. The [[Species/Legends|species]] was capable of seeing up to twenty [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in complete darkness, although they were unable to distinguish color under those conditions. Starweirds could use the Force powers [[Tutaminis|Drain energy]], [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force grip]], [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]], and [[Force sight]]. They had no ecological role, and after [[Death/Legends|dying]], a starweird left no traces of itself behind.<ref name="UA" />

==Behavior==
Starweirds would typically appear to [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] repairing their damaged [[Starship/Legends|starship]] in deep space, or manifest aboard a ship traveling in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. Upon being spotted, starweirds became enraged and released a loud, piercing [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathic]] shriek that affected creatures within twenty meters. Due to the call's telepathic nature, it could be heard even in the vacuum of space. Their scream often caused listeners to cower in fear or attempt to flee, although some individuals were able to overcome their terror and fight back. After issuing the shriek, the powerful creature would set upon its foe, shredding them with its sharp claws. A starweird would choose one target and focus on that individual. The creatures particularly hated Force-sensitives, whom they would mindlessly concentrate on killing even if other creatures were present.<ref name="UA" />

==History==
Starweirds were found solely in deep space. They were considered a mysterious species, and some [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] hypothesized that they were physical manifestations of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. However, little available evidence supported the hypothesis.<ref name="UA" /> During the [[Great Galactic War|first war]] between the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the [[Starweird Queen]] was a member of the species who was considered to be legendary. The Starweird [[Gender/Legends|Queen]] [[Defeat of the Starweird Queen|attacked]] many of the members of the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] and a [[Padawan/Legends|Jedi Padawan]] named [[Xerender]]. The group of Jedi was saved by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Wyellett]], who was the teacher of Xerender, which caused the Jedi Master to be captured by Imperial forces.<ref name="TOR">{{TORcite|type=codex|Master Wyellett (Warrior)}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
An unnamed creature with a description identical to that of a Starweird was first mentioned in ''[[Tanith: the Guest-Star Wars]]'', an unlicensed [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] article published in the French magazine ''[[Graal 24]]'' in [[1990]]. They were described as incredible creatures living in hyperspace that hunted Force-sensitives and left large claw marks on the hulls of ships.<ref name="GuestStar">{{GraalCite|24|Tanith: the Guest-Star Wars}}</ref> 

Starweirds were first officially created for ''[[Ultimate Adversaries]]'', a [[2004]] sourcebook written by [[Eric Cagle]], [[Michelle Lyons]], [[Michael Mikaelian]], [[Steve Miller]], [[Owen K.C. Stephens]], and [[Wil Upchurch]] for [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Revised Core Rulebook|revised edition]] of the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]''. A picture of a starweird was drawn for the sourcebook by [[Andrew Jones]].<ref name="UA" /> In ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', a [[2011]] [[Star Wars video games|MMORPG]] produced by [[BioWare]], an entity known as the "Starweird Queen" was mentioned in the codex entry for Master Wyellett, which was given to members of the [[Sith Warrior]] class on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. The entry did not specify where the battle between the Starweird Queen and the Jedi took place, or what happened to the Queen at the end of the battle.<ref name="TOR" />
